author: Tunstall, 1771
status: 나그네새 수만 마리 · 겨울철새 수천 마리

months.note: 9월 하순에 찾아와 이듬해 5월 중순까지 머물거나 지나가며, 4~5월 이동기에 가장 많다.

summary: 겨울에 찾아와 머물거나 지나가는 겨울철새로, 논과 풀밭, 해안, 하천에서 지낸다. 몸집이 작고 날씬하며 꼬리와 다리가 길다. 무리를 지어 다니며 풀씨와 곤충을 먹는다. 북반구 고위도에서 번식하고, 겨울에는 우리나라와 중국 동남부, 일본, 미국 남부, 멕시코 등지에서 지낸다.
young: 첫가을 어린새는 어른새보다 윗면이 더 어둡고 갈색을 띠며, 아랫면은 연한 누런빛 바탕에 가슴과 옆구리의 검은 얼룩과 세로줄이 더 굵다.

similar.how: 옅은밭종다리는 아랫면이 더 희고 가슴 줄무늬가 갈색으로 흐리며 다리가 검은빛을 띠지만, 밭종다리는 가슴과 옆구리에 검은 세로줄이 굵고 뚜렷하며 다리가 살구빛이다.

art.subject: American Pipit (Anthus rubescens) of the Asian subspecies japonicus (Buff-bellied Pipit), adult in winter plumage, as seen in Korea from November to March: crown and upperparts grey-brown with only faint dark streaks; a whitish supercilium and pale lores giving an open-faced look; a bold blackish malar stripe broadening into a dark patch on the side of the throat; two whitish wing-bars; underparts white with a faint buff wash, the breast and flanks boldly streaked black; dark brown tail with white outer tail feathers. Thin dark bill with a pinkish base to the lower mandible; dark eye; reddish flesh-coloured legs.
art.pose: walking on a paddy bund, picking seeds and insects, a small flock nearby
art.scene: Korean winter rice paddies: harvested stubble fields beside a river; no people, buildings or text
views: adult winter, side view walking on a paddy bund: faintly streaked grey-brown upperparts, whitish supercilium, two whitish wing-bars, white underparts boldly streaked black on breast and flanks, long dark tail, reddish flesh-coloured legs
adult winter, head detail in side view: pale lores, whitish supercilium, bold blackish malar stripe, thin dark bill with a pinkish base to the lower mandible
art.build: Small, slender pipit, about 16cm, a little longer than a sparrow, with a long tail and fairly long legs; horizontal stance, walks steadily over wet fields and pumps its tail up and down. Bill thin, straight and pointed, shorter than the head. Legs reddish flesh-pink, medium length, with a moderately long hind claw. Tail long and square-ended, dark with white outer feathers that show in flight. Usually in small flocks on paddies, riverbanks and shores.
avoid: Do not paint heavy black-and-white streaks on the back or a streaked rump; that is Red-throated Pipit (Anthus cervinus), which also has a pinkish-red throat in spring.
Do not paint dark brown or blackish legs; this Asian form has pale reddish-pink legs.
Do not give it an olive-green back with a white-and-black spot on the ear-coverts; that is Olive-backed Pipit (Anthus hodgsoni).
Do not make the streaks below fine and brown; they are bold and black on a white ground.
